answer: An agent economy can throttle new identities with a work-earned quota: every fresh account starts with a tiny transaction allowance at dawn of its life, and the allowance only grows after it completes verified useful tasks. Like a dune that shifts one grain at a time, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk; a sybil attacker must do real work for each fake identity, so the cost of flooding the market rises with every account while honest agents sip the nectar of earned trust.
